trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Vatican City, Borgo district Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use the time to rest on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 13:00. Take the Leonardo Express train to Roma Termini (€14, ~32 min), then connect via metro or bus to the Vatican/Borgo district. Check in to your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation stroll through the charming Borgo district streets leading toward Castel Sant'Angelo. Admire the castle's exterior and the beautiful Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge lined with angel statues — both free to view from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Wander along the Tiber riverbank at sunset for atmospheric views. Explore the Prati neighborhood (a short walk from Borgo) — a lively, authentic Roman district with great street energy.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick coffee and cornetto (croissant) at the airport bar for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick slice of Roman pizza al taglio near Termini station or in Prati — budget €4–6 per person.
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzarium-style meal in Prati neighborhood. Try 'Il Sorpasso' or any local trattoria with a fixed-price 'menu del giorno' for €10–15 including pasta and water.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour Roma Pass or simply use single bus/metro tickets (€1.50 each). Validate tickets before boarding. June in Rome is warm (25–32°C), so pack light clothes and sunscreen. The Borgo district is extremely well-located — Vatican Museums, St. Peter's, and Castel Sant'Angelo are all within 10–15 minutes on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Early start is essential! Head to the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel — book tickets online in advance (€17–20) to skip the notoriously long queues. Arrive right at opening (8:00 AM). Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and the breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling by Michelangelo. This is a world-class art experience at a very reasonable price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit the Vatican Museums and walk directly into St. Peter's Basilica — entry is completely FREE. Marvel at Michelangelo's Pietà, Bernini's massive bronze baldachin, and the grand interior. For €8, climb the dome of St. Peter's (stairs option) for one of Rome's most spectacular panoramic views. Afterward, relax in St. Peter's Square.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back through Borgo Pio — a picturesque medieval lane lined with cafes and restaurants — for a classic Roman evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a classic Roman breakfast at a local bar near your hotel: espresso + cornetto for €1.50–2.50. Avoid sitting down at tourist cafes near the Vatican to keep costs low.
meals.lunch: Eat before or after the Vatican at 'Forno Borgo' or similar bakeries on Borgo Pio for fresh sandwiches and supplì (fried rice balls) — budget €5–8.
meals.dinner: Dine at a trattoria on Borgo Pio or Via della Conciliazione. Look for restaurants offering 'pasta + secondi + house wine' deals for €12–18. Try cacio e pepe or carbonara — authentic Roman pasta dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-booking Vatican tickets online is strongly recommended, especially in June (peak season). Free entry to St. Peter's Basilica requires modest dress — shoulders and knees must be covered; bring a scarf or light cardigan. The dome climb has two options: elevator partway + stairs (€8) or all stairs (€6).

day_by_day.morning: Take bus 40 or 64 (€1.50) from near the Vatican to the historic center. Visit the Pantheon — one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings. Entry is now €5. Spend time inside admiring the perfect dome and oculus. Afterward, walk 5 minutes to the stunning Piazza Navona — free to enter — with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers as the centerpiece. Great for people-watching and street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Campo de' Fiori market (mornings only, but the square is lively all day) and then continue to the Jewish Ghetto — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhoods. Explore the medieval streets, free synagogue exterior, and Portico d'Ottavia ruins. Walk across to Trastevere neighborhood — Rome's most bohemian and photogenic quarter — for afternoon exploration of its cobblestone lanes and colorful buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Trastevere for the evening — this neighborhood comes alive after dark with locals and students. Browse the artisan shops and street musicians.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a local bar near your hotel — €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab street food near Campo de' Fiori or in the Jewish Ghetto — try supplì, artichokes alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes), or a simple panino — budget €5–8.
meals.dinner: Trastevere has excellent budget trattorias. Try 'Da Enzo al 29' or 'Tonnarello' for authentic Roman cuisine — pasta dishes €8–12, full meal with wine €15–20. Arrive early (7:00–7:30 PM) to avoid queues.

day_by_day.notes: Bus 40 or 64 from Lungotevere near Castel Sant'Angelo connects directly to the historic center. Trastevere is best explored on foot. The neighborhood is roughly 20–25 minutes walk from the Vatican or a short bus ride (bus 23 along the Tiber). Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded tourist areas.

day_by_day.morning: Today is dedicated to Ancient Rome. Take the metro (Line B from Termini or bus from the center) to the Colosseum. Book tickets online in advance — combined Colosseum + Roman Forum + Palatine Hill ticket costs €16. Spend 1.5 hours at the Colosseum exploring the iconic amphitheater where gladiators once fought.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use your combined ticket to walk through the Roman Forum and up to Palatine Hill — included in the same €16 ticket. These sprawling ancient ruins are extraordinary and often less crowded than the Colosseum. Take your time among the temples, arches, and ancient streets. Nearby, the Circus Maximus (free to view from outside) is a short walk away.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up to the Aventine Hill (free) to find the famous Knights of Malta keyhole — peek through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Then enjoy the peaceful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for sunset views over Rome.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and cornetto at your neighborhood bar — €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local alimentari (deli) or supermarket near your hotel — buy fresh bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit for €5–7. Eat in the shade near the Forum or Circus Maximus.
meals.dinner: Head to the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's traditional working-class food district. Try 'Flavio al Velavevodetto' or explore the Testaccio Market area for authentic Roman offal dishes (try trippa or coda alla vaccinara) or simple pasta. Budget €12–18 for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: June heat can be intense by midday — start the Colosseum early (opening is 9:00 AM). Bring a refillable water bottle; Rome has hundreds of free drinking fountains called 'nasoni' throughout the city — the water is clean and cold. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the Forum terrain is uneven ancient cobblestone.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art museums, housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings. IMPORTANT: Reservations are mandatory and must be booked weeks in advance (€15 entry + €2 booking fee). Visits are in strict 2-hour time slots. Take bus 910 from Termini or walk through Villa Borghese park. After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's central park — which are completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down from Villa Borghese to the Spanish Steps (Piazza di Spagna) — free to visit, though sitting on the steps is now restricted. Toss a coin in the nearby Trevi Fountain (free to visit, coin toss optional!). This is Rome's most famous fountain and a must-see. Continue to the Quirinal Hill area for views over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively streets around Via del Corso and the historic center for evening passeggiata (the Italian tradition of an evening stroll). Window-shop, people-watch, and soak up the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bar breakfast near hotel — espresso + cornetto €2–3.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — buy supplies from a nearby alimentari or supermarket. Budget €6–8 for a lovely alfresco lunch under the trees.
meals.dinner: Explore the area around Piazza del Popolo or Via della Croce near the Spanish Steps for dinner. Look for fixed-price tourist menus (avoid the most touristy spots right on the piazza) — aim for €12–18 for pasta and a secondo. Alternatively, grab excellent pizza al taglio for €5–8.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery booking is absolutely essential — this is one of Rome's most popular museums and sells out weeks ahead, especially in June. If you haven't pre-booked, substitute with a visit to the free Capitoline Museums courtyard or the MAXXI modern art museum (€12). The Trevi Fountain area is very crowded; visit early morning or late evening for better photos.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but fascinating neighborhood of Pigneto or take a morning food market experience at Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (open Saturday mornings, free entry) — one of Europe's largest and most atmospheric flea markets. Great for vintage finds, street food, and local color. Alternatively, visit the beautiful Santa Maria Maggiore Basilica (free entry) — one of Rome's four major basilicas with stunning mosaics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15) — the world's oldest public museums, sitting atop Capitoline Hill with incredible views of the Roman Forum. See the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, Capitoline Wolf sculpture, and outstanding Roman antiquities. The terrace offers one of the best free views of the Forum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Borgo/Vatican neighborhood for a final evening stroll. Walk along the Tiber at the golden hour and enjoy the illuminated Castel Sant'Angelo — spectacular at night.

meals.breakfast: Try a different local bar for your morning coffee ritual — explore Prati neighborhood's bars for authentic Roman breakfast culture. €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab street food at Porta Portese market or a simple trattoria lunch in Trastevere — budget €8–12 for pasta and a drink.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your second-to-last evening — find a well-reviewed trattoria in Prati (your home neighborhood) for a proper Roman dinner: antipasto, pasta, main course, house wine — budget €20–25 per person. Try 'Osteria dell'Angelo' in Prati for authentic cacio e pepe and Roman classics.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is market day across Rome — Porta Portese (Trastevere) and Campo de' Fiori are particularly lively. The Capitoline Museums are a great alternative if Borghese was missed. Many churches in Rome are free to enter and contain world-class art — Santa Maria sopra Minerva (near the Pantheon) has Michelangelo's 'Christ the Redeemer' statue and beautiful Fra Angelico frescoes, completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Sunday morning in Rome is magical. Head to St. Peter's Square for the Papal Angelus blessing — every Sunday at noon the Pope (or a representative) appears at the window above St. Peter's Square to address the crowd. Completely free and a unique cultural/spiritual experience regardless of your beliefs. Arrive by 11:30 AM to get a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Angelus, visit the free Castel Sant'Angelo interior (€15.50 entry) — the cylindrical fortress with a fascinating history as papal refuge, prison, and military stronghold. Excellent views from the top terrace over Rome and St. Peter's. Alternatively, if budget is tight, simply enjoy the exterior and bridge for free. Spend your last afternoon doing any missed sights or souvenir shopping in Prati.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Rome — enjoy a leisurely last dinner in the Borgo or Prati neighborhood. Pack your bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman bar breakfast — try a maritozzo (cream-filled sweet bun, a Roman specialty) with your espresso. €3–4.
meals.lunch: After the Angelus, grab a casual lunch near the Vatican — try 'Pizzarium' by Gabriele Bonci in Prati (Via della Meloria 43) — widely considered Rome's best pizza al taglio, sold by weight. Budget €8–12 for a satisfying lunch.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — choose your favorite spot from the week or try a new Prati trattoria. Toast to Rome with a glass of local Frascati white wine or a Peroni beer. Budget €15–20 for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan accordingly — if departing on June 21, ensure your hotel checkout and transfer to the airport are arranged. Leonardo Express from Roma Termini to Fiumicino runs every 30 minutes and takes 32 minutes (€14). Budget tip: the cheaper FL1 regional train also connects Termini to the airport for €8 but takes slightly longer. Leave at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Boutique Stay in the Borgo district (Vatican City area). After freshening up, take a leisurely orientation stroll through the Borgo neighborhood. Walk along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square for your first breathtaking view of the basilica's facade and Bernini's colonnade. No tickets needed — simply soak in the atmosphere and get your bearings around the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Prati neighborhood, a short walk from Borgo, for your first Roman dinner. Browse the lively streets and settle in for the evening.

meals.breakfast: On the plane / airport snack before landing
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or at Fiumicino — try a panino or pizza al taglio at a airport café (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Sorpasso in Prati — a beloved local spot serving classic Roman antipasti, pasta, and natural wines. Mid-range, expect €30–40 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a transit card (Roma Pass or rechargeable MetreRoma card) at a tabacchi near the hotel. June in Rome is warm and sunny (typically 25–30°C), so pack light layers and sunscreen for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Your hotel's prime location makes this a 10-minute walk. Pre-booked timed entry tickets are essential (book online in advance, €20–27). Arrive at opening (8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry, separate queue). Climb the dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot). Then cross the Tiber via Ponte Sant'Angelo to visit Castel Sant'Angelo — a striking fortress with medieval history and rooftop views (€15 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Relax back in the Borgo/Prati area. Enjoy an aperitivo hour — a Roman tradition of pre-dinner drinks with free snacks — at a bar on Via Cola di Rienzo.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby cornetto e cappuccino at Bar San Pietro (a classic local bar steps from the Vatican, €3–5)
meals.lunch: Trattoria Da Settimio all'Arancio near Castel Sant'Angelo — hearty Roman lunch with cacio e pepe and carciofi alla romana (€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — a no-frills Roman trattoria famous for its fixed-price dinner of traditional dishes like rigatoni alla pajata and abbacchio. Approx €25–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets sell out weeks in advance in June — book as soon as possible if not already done. Dress code enforced at St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees required. Arrive at the Vatican by 8:00 AM to maximize your morning.

day_by_day.morning: Pasta Making Class in the Historic Center — Take Bus 40 or 64 from Borgo to the historic center (15 min). Join a hands-on morning cooking class (typically 10:00 AM–1:00 PM, €65–85 per person) led by a local Roman chef. Learn to make fresh cacio e pepe, tonnarelli, and perhaps a Roman dessert. You'll eat what you make — a delicious and interactive cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the class, walk to the nearby Pantheon (€5 entry, pre-book online) — one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world. Then meander through Piazza Navona with its baroque fountains and street artists. Browse the antique shops and boutiques around Campo de' Fiori.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Campo de' Fiori area as it transforms into a vibrant evening scene. Have a gelato at Giolitti or Fatamorgana (artisan flavors) before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local bar — cornetto integrale with a macchiato (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Included in the pasta making class — you eat the meal you prepare!
meals.dinner: Trattoria Moderna near Campo de' Fiori — excellent Roman cuisine with a contemporary touch. Try the supplì, pasta alla gricia, and tiramisu. Budget €35–45 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — the historic center involves a lot of cobblestone walking. The cooking class location will be confirmed upon booking; most are a short walk from Piazza Navona. Carry a reusable water bottle — Rome's nasoni (street fountains) offer free, clean drinking water throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Take a taxi or Bus 910 to Villa Borghese (25–30 min from Borgo). Timed entry is mandatory and strictly enforced (book well in advance, €15 + €2 booking fee). Spend 2 hours marveling at Bernini's masterpieces — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — alongside Caravaggio's dramatic canvases. This intimate gallery is one of Rome's greatest artistic treasures.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's central park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€5 for 20 min) or simply relax under the pines. Walk down the Spanish Steps to the Trevi Fountain (toss a coin!). Explore the elegant Via Condotti shopping street — window shopping is free!
day_by_day.evening: Wander the atmospheric streets around the Trevi Fountain and Piazza di Spagna as the golden hour light bathes the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Caffè Greco on Via Condotti (Rome's oldest café, est. 1760) — a splurge-worthy cappuccino experience (€6–8 at the bar)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, cheese, prosciutto, and fruit from a nearby alimentari or Mercato Trionfale (Rome's largest covered market, near your hotel). Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Nino near the Spanish Steps — a classic Roman institution beloved by locals and discerning visitors since 1934. Excellent ribollita, pasta, and Florentine steak. €40–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery allows only 360 visitors per 2-hour slot — this is non-negotiable. Book tickets the moment they become available (usually 2–3 months ahead). The gallery is closed on Mondays. From the gallery, the Spanish Steps area is walkable downhill through the park in about 25 minutes — a lovely route.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Ruins — Take Bus 40 or 64 to Largo Argentina, then walk (or take Metro B to Colosseo). Combined ticket covers the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill (€18, pre-book to skip queues). Start at the Forum at 9:00 AM before the heat peaks — walk where Julius Caesar was assassinated, see the Temple of Vesta, and climb Palatine Hill for sweeping views over ancient Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum (included in combined ticket) — the iconic amphitheater that once held 50,000 spectators. Afterward, walk to the Circus Maximus and the Aventine Hill. Visit the Knights of Malta keyhole on Aventine Hill for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome — a free and magical hidden gem.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic working-class food district — for an early evening exploration of its market and streets.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto in Trastevere (nearby) — a no-frills Roman bar with excellent espresso and cornetti. Very local, very cheap (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Pizzarium Bonci near the Forum area — Gabriele Bonci's legendary pizza al taglio with creative seasonal toppings, sold by weight. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — a celebrated trattoria built into Monte dei Cocci (a hill of ancient amphorae shards). Superb cacio e pepe, carbonara, and coda alla vaccinara. €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: June heat can be intense by midday — start the Forum early (9:00 AM opening) and wear a hat and sunscreen. Carry water. The Colosseum interior can be hot; the Forum is largely exposed. The Aventine Hill keyhole is at Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta — there's often a short queue but it moves quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — sleep in and enjoy a slow Roman Saturday. Visit the weekly Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (open 6:00 AM–2:00 PM, free entry) — one of Rome's largest and most famous markets, selling antiques, vintage clothing, books, and curiosities. A wonderful cultural experience even if you don't buy anything.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (afternoon session if available, or explore independently) — Wander through Trastevere's enchanting cobblestone streets. Visit the magnificent Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free, stunning 12th-century mosaics). Browse artisan shops and soak up the neighborhood's bohemian character. Cross the Tiber to visit the Jewish Ghetto and taste the neighborhood's unique Roman-Jewish cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join the guided evening food tour through Trastevere (€65–85 per person, 3 hours). Sample supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes, porchetta, local cheeses, and paired wines while your guide shares stories of Roman history and culinary tradition. This is the highlight food experience of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Forno Campo de' Fiori — take a short bus ride for Rome's most celebrated bakery. Try the pizza bianca (€2–3) and a fresh pastry.
meals.lunch: Sora Margherita in the Jewish Ghetto — a tiny, legendary trattoria with no sign on the door, serving Roman-Jewish classics like carciofi alla giudia and pasta e ceci. Cash only, ~€25 per person. Arrive early — it fills fast.
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — multiple tastings of street food, snacks, and wine pairings across several stops. A light post-tour gelato at Fatamorgana Trastevere to finish the night.

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese is extremely crowded on Saturday mornings — keep valuables secure and be aware of pickpockets. The Trastevere food walk typically departs around 6:30–7:00 PM — confirm exact meeting point with your tour operator upon booking. Saturday evenings in Trastevere are lively and festive.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast. Then visit the nearby Castel Sant'Angelo gardens or take a final walk along the Tiber riverbanks. Pop into any churches you haven't yet visited — Rome's churches are free and filled with masterpieces (try Sant'Agostino for Caravaggio's Madonna dei Pellegrini, or Santa Maria del Popolo for more Caravaggios and a Raphael chapel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in Prati (Via Cola di Rienzo) — pick up local pasta, olive oil, truffle products, or artisan gifts. Return to the hotel for final packing. Depending on departure time, arrange an airport transfer (taxi from Borgo to Fiumicino is approximately €50–55 fixed rate, or take the Leonardo Express train from Roma Termini, €14).
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final dinner if schedule allows.

meals.breakfast: A leisurely Roman breakfast at Sciascia Caffè in Prati — one of Rome's most storied historic cafés, famous for its thick hot chocolate and perfect espresso. A fitting farewell ritual (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Pizzarium or a final Roman pizza al taglio near the hotel — a casual, delicious send-off (€10–15).
meals.dinner: If departing late: Dal Toscano in Prati — a reliable, warmly-reviewed trattoria near your hotel for a final sit-down Roman meal of bistecca, pasta, and house wine (€35–45 per person). If departing early evening, grab a panino from a local forno for the journey.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the transfer to Fiumicino (traffic can be heavy on Sunday evenings). Pre-book your airport taxi or arrange through your hotel. Leave a review for your boutique stay — small hotels thrive on guest feedback. Arrivederci, Roma!

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Private chauffeur transfer from the airport to your boutique stay in the Borgo district, Vatican City. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation stroll through the Borgo district and along the banks of the Tiber River. Explore the charming medieval streets surrounding Castel Sant'Angelo, admiring the fortress exterior and the iconic Ponte Sant'Angelo with its angel statues — a perfect, low-key introduction to Rome just steps from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive dinner reservation at Il Sorpasso or Ristorante Il Matriciano, both celebrated Prati-district establishments beloved by Romans. Enjoy classic Roman cuisine — cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara — paired with a curated wine list in an intimate, sophisticated setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Late afternoon aperitivo and light bites at a wine bar near Castel Sant'Angelo — try Enoteca Il Sorpasso for charcuterie, cheeses, and a glass of natural Roman white wine.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Matriciano (Via dei Gracchi) — a historic trattoria with impeccable Roman classics; reserve the private corner table for a premium experience.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Ask the hotel concierge to confirm all upcoming reservations and arrange private skip-the-line entry for the Vatican Museums on Day 2. June weather in Rome is warm (25–32°C); carry water and light layers for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Private early-access guided tour starting at 08:00 before general crowds arrive. Explore the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminate in an awe-inspiring, near-private viewing of Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling. Your expert art historian guide will bring every fresco to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit St. Peter's Basilica immediately after the Museums via the internal passage (exclusive to private tours). Ascend to the top of St. Peter's Dome for panoramic views over Rome. Afterward, return to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest during the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Pasta Making Class in the Historic Center — Join a premium hands-on cooking class led by a celebrated local Roman chef. Master fresh cacio e pepe, tonnarelli, and Roman pasta traditions in a beautifully appointed kitchen space. Enjoy the meal you've created with premium wines as part of the class.

meals.breakfast: Full Italian breakfast at the hotel — cornetti, freshly squeezed blood orange juice, espresso, and seasonal fruit.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio near the Vatican — a refined spot for grilled branzino, Roman artichokes, and a chilled Frascati white.
meals.dinner: Dinner is included as part of the Pasta Making Class experience — a convivial multi-course Roman feast with wine pairings in the chef's private dining space.

day_by_day.notes: The Vatican Museums private early-access tour must be booked well in advance — confirm with your concierge. Wear comfortable walking shoes; the Museums cover over 7 km of galleries. The cooking class is typically located in the Centro Storico, a short taxi or private car ride from the Borgo district.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Private guided visit to the Villa Borghese, home to Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's most dramatic canvases. Entry is strictly timed and limited, making this one of Rome's most exclusive art experiences. Arrive at 09:00 for the first slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's most elegant park — before descending to the Spanish Steps and the Tridente neighborhood. Browse the luxury boutiques along Via Condotti (Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi) and explore the Piazza del Popolo and its twin baroque churches.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — A premium guided gastronomy tour through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere. Sample supplì (Roman fried rice balls), artisan pizza al taglio, cured meats, aged pecorino, and local Castelli Romani wines as you wander through one of Rome's most atmospheric neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel followed by an espresso at a local Prati bar — stand at the counter like a true Roman.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Caffè delle Arti inside the Villa Borghese gardens — a sophisticated terrace restaurant with views of the park; try the burrata with heirloom tomatoes and fresh pasta.
meals.dinner: The Trastevere Food & Wine Walk serves as a progressive dinner. Conclude the evening with a nightcap of limoncello or Amaro at a candlelit Trastevere wine bar such as Enoteca Ferrara.

day_by_day.notes: The Borghese Gallery only admits 360 visitors per two-hour slot — pre-booking is mandatory and sells out weeks in advance. The gallery is a short taxi ride or a scenic walk through the Borghese park from the Borgo district. Wear comfortable shoes for the evening Trastevere walk on cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Ruins — Private guided archaeological tour of the ancient heart of Rome. Walk the Forum where Julius Caesar addressed the Senate, explore the House of Augustus with its remarkably preserved frescoes, and stand atop Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Colosseum and the Circus Maximus. Begin at 08:30 to beat the midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum with your private guide, including exclusive access to the arena floor and underground hypogeum (where gladiators and animals were held). Afterward, explore the Capitoline Hill and the world's oldest public museums — the Capitoline Museums — housing the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue and Caravaggio masterpieces.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the Capitoline Hill terrace with views over the Forum, followed by a premium dinner reservation in the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's true culinary heartland.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with a focus on seasonal Roman produce — ricotta with honey, prosciutto di Parma, and freshly baked bread.
meals.lunch: A light lunch at Ristorante Aroma, the Michelin-starred rooftop restaurant of the Palazzo Manfredi hotel, with direct views of the Colosseum — one of Rome's most spectacular dining settings.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — a beloved institution serving authentic Roman offal dishes and robust pastas in a cave-like setting carved into Monte dei Cocci (a hill of ancient amphorae shards).

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum underground and arena floor require advance booking for special access. June heat can be intense by midday — start early, carry water, and wear a hat and sunscreen. The Testaccio neighborhood is a short taxi ride from the Forum area.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private art tour of Rome's baroque churches — a curated walk through some of the world's greatest free art galleries: San Luigi dei Francesi (three Caravaggio masterpieces), Sant'Agostino (another Caravaggio), and Santa Maria della Vittoria (Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa). Your private art historian guide provides context that transforms these spaces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Piazza Navona and the Pantheon — visit the perfectly preserved Roman temple (now a church) and marvel at its 2,000-year-old unreinforced concrete dome. Wander through the Campo de' Fiori market (winding down by afternoon) and the Jewish Ghetto, visiting the Great Synagogue and tasting Roman Jewish cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Premium dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant in the Centro Storico — Il Pagliaccio (two Michelin stars) offers a stunning tasting menu blending Italian tradition with avant-garde technique, paired with an exceptional wine journey curated by their sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a mid-morning coffee at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè — widely considered Rome's finest espresso bar, near the Pantheon.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Piperno in the Jewish Ghetto — a historic institution famous for carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style deep-fried artichokes), baccalà, and Roman Jewish specialties.
meals.dinner: Il Pagliaccio (Via dei Banchi Vecchi) — Two Michelin stars; reserve the chef's table for an immersive, personalized tasting menu experience with premium wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Book Il Pagliaccio well in advance — it is one of Rome's most sought-after reservations. The morning church tour is best done before 10:00 when light streams through the windows most beautifully. Ask your guide to time the visit to San Luigi dei Francesi for optimal lighting on the Caravaggio canvases.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to the Castelli Romani wine country — the volcanic hills south of Rome that have supplied the city with wine since antiquity. Visit a premium winery in Frascati or Castel Gandolfo for an exclusive cellar tour and guided tasting of Malvasia and other local varietals, paired with local cheeses and cured meats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Castel Gandolfo — the papal summer residence perched above Lake Albano — for a private guided tour of the Papal Palace gardens (now open to the public). Stroll through the charming hilltop village and enjoy the cooler air and stunning lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome by private car in time for a sunset stroll across Ponte Sant'Angelo and along the Tiber embankment. Final evening dinner at a rooftop restaurant with panoramic Roman views — a celebratory penultimate night.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for the Castelli Romani.
meals.lunch: Long, leisurely winery lunch — a full spread of antipasti, seasonal pasta, grilled meats, and estate wines at the vineyard's private dining terrace.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Settimo, the rooftop restaurant of the Sofitel Rome Villa Borghese — exceptional Italian cuisine with a sweeping 360° panorama of Rome's skyline at dusk.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car and driver for the full Castelli Romani day — approximately 30–45 minutes from Rome. This is an excellent day to escape the city crowds, as Saturday brings more tourists to central Rome. The winery visit should be pre-arranged through your hotel concierge for a truly exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent hotel breakfast. Take a peaceful early walk to St. Peter's Square to witness the Sunday atmosphere, potentially catching the Papal Angelus blessing (delivered by the Pope at noon from his window overlooking the square — a unique Roman experience).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last exploration of the Prati neighborhood — Rome's elegant early-20th-century quarter surrounding your hotel. Browse the gourmet food shops along Via Cola di Rienzo for premium Italian provisions to bring home: aged Parmigiano, truffle products, artisan pasta, and fine wines. Visit the Mercato Trionfale — Rome's largest covered food market — for a final immersion in Roman culinary culture.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Ristorante La Pergola — Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, perched atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel with unparalleled panoramic views of the Eternal City. Chef Heinz Beck's legendary tasting menu is a transcendent finale to a week of world-class dining. Reserve months in advance.

meals.breakfast: Grand hotel breakfast — the full spread, savored slowly as a final Roman morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Pizzarium Bonci in Prati — Gabriele Bonci's legendary pizza al taglio shop, considered the finest in Rome; a perfect, casual counterpoint to the week's fine dining.
meals.dinner: La Pergola at Rome Cavalieri (Via Alberto Cadlolo) — Three Michelin stars; book the window table for the full panoramic Rome experience. The tasting menu with wine pairing is the ultimate luxury farewell to Rome.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola requires reservations made months ahead — ensure your concierge secures this on your behalf before the trip. If departing the following morning, arrange a pre-dawn or early private transfer to the airport. Pack your gourmet provisions carefully to comply with customs regulations. Consider tipping your guides, drivers, and hotel staff generously — Roman hospitality at this level is exceptional.
